*Bertelsmann Expects 2026 EBITDA Including Synergies to Amount to EUR3.8B
Bertelsmann Lifts Guidance After Growth in Key Units
Media group Bertelsmann raised its full-year guidance after it reported higher revenue in the first half of the year, boosted by growth across its key divisions.
The German company, which houses Penguin Random House and RTL Group, now expects full-year group revenue at around 22 billion euros ($25.63 billion) instead of more than 20 billion euros.
It also projects earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization including synergies to amount to 3.8 billion euros, the company said Friday.

"RTL Group's streaming business will be profitable and make a substantial contribution of around 120 million euros to Bertelsmann's operating Ebitda adjusted this year," Chief Executive Officer Thomas Rabe said.

For the first half, revenue rose to 9.30 billion euros from 9.08 billion euros for the same period a year earlier, reflecting growth in some of its main segments including Penguin Random House, Bertelsmann Music Group and Arvato Group.
Adjusted operating earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization increased to 1.31 billion euros from 1.25 billion euros.
Meanwhile, profit rose to 292 million euros from 201 million euros.
